stem: At this rate, by how many square centimeters does the mat's area increase each hour?
stimulus: An ecologist monitoring a farm pond finds that a floating mat of duckweed is expanding at a constant rate of $0.45$ square meters per day. ($1$ meter $= 100$ centimeters and $1$ day $= 24$ hours.)
explanation: Make both changes inside one chain and check that the units cancel. Square meters become square centimeters, so you apply the linear factor twice: $1\text{ m}^2 = (100\text{ cm})^2 = 10{,}000\text{ cm}^2$. Days become hours, and because the day is in the denominator, you divide by 24. $0.45\,\frac{\text{m}^2}{\text{day}} \times \frac{10{,}000\text{ cm}^2}{1\text{ m}^2} \times \frac{1\text{ day}}{24\text{ hours}} = \frac{4500}{24} = 187.5$ square centimeters per hour. Students commonly get these wrong answers: 1.875 (using 100 instead of 10,000 for the area), 4500 (converting the area but leaving the rate per day), 108000 (multiplying by 24 instead of dividing).

common_errors.why: Applied the linear factor once (0.45 × 100 ÷ 24) instead of squaring it to 10,000 for square units.
Converted square meters to square centimeters but stopped before changing 'per day' to 'per hour'.
Multiplied by 24 instead of dividing. 'Per day' is in the denominator, so going to hours makes the rate smaller.

stem: According to the folklorist's conversion, what is the courier's speed, in leagues per hour?
stimulus: A folklorist studying a regional legend about a tireless night courier finds that one version of the tale says the courier ran at a steady $90$ furlongs per hour. In the measurement system the tale uses, $1$ league $= 3$ miles and $1$ mile $= 8$ furlongs. The folklorist wants to compare this speed with another version of the tale that gives speeds in leagues per hour.
explanation: Only the distance unit changes. 'Per hour' stays as it is, so don't touch it. A league is $3 \times 8 = 24$ furlongs, which makes a league the larger unit, so the number has to get smaller. $90\,\frac{\text{furlongs}}{\text{hour}} \times \frac{1\text{ mile}}{8\text{ furlongs}} \times \frac{1\text{ league}}{3\text{ miles}} = \frac{90}{24} = 3.75$ leagues per hour. Students commonly get these wrong answers: 11.25 (stopping at miles per hour), 2160 (multiplying by the factors instead of dividing), 30 (dividing by 3 only and skipping the furlong-to-mile step), 0.0625 (also changing hours to minutes, which the question didn't ask for).

common_errors.why: Converted furlongs to miles (90 ÷ 8) but didn't go on to convert miles to leagues.
Flipped the conversion and multiplied (90 × 8 × 3), so furlongs didn't cancel.
Used only the 3 miles per league and skipped the 8 furlongs per mile (90 ÷ 3).
Converted both parts of the rate, giving leagues per minute (3.75 ÷ 60) when the time unit was meant to stay as hours.

stem: At this rate, how many hours will it take the team to sieve all of the soil from the test pit?
stimulus: An archaeology field team digs a rectangular test pit that is $6$ feet long, $4.5$ feet wide, and $6$ feet deep. All of the soil removed from the pit must go through a screening sieve. The team's sieving station processes soil at a constant rate of $0.75$ cubic yard per hour. ($1$ yard $= 3$ feet.)
explanation: First find the volume of the pit in cubic feet: $6 \times 4.5 \times 6 = 162$ cubic feet. The sieving rate is in cubic yards, so convert the volume. A cubic yard is $3^3 = 27$ cubic feet, so you apply the linear factor three times: $162 \div 27 = 6$ cubic yards. Then divide by the rate: $6\text{ yd}^3 \div 0.75\,\frac{\text{yd}^3}{\text{hour}} = 8$ hours. Check the last line: the question asks for hours, not volume. Students commonly get these wrong answers: 72 (dividing by 3 instead of 27), 24 (dividing by 9), 216 (not converting at all), 6 (stopping at the volume).

common_errors.why: Applied the linear factor once (162 ÷ 3 = 54 'cubic yards') instead of cubing it, then divided by 0.75.
Squared the factor instead of cubing it (162 ÷ 9 = 18), then divided by 0.75.
Divided 162 cubic feet directly by a rate given in cubic yards per hour, without converting.
Found the volume in cubic yards correctly but gave it as the answer instead of the time.

stem: To the nearest tenth of a gram, what is the weight of the panel?
stimulus: A textile historian examining a nineteenth-century silk mill's records finds that one of its brocades was woven to a weight of $50$ grams per square yard. A surviving rectangular panel of this brocade measures $2.5$ feet by $1.4$ feet. ($1$ yard $= 3$ feet.)
explanation: The panel's area is $2.5 \times 1.4 = 3.5$ square feet. A square yard is $3^2 = 9$ square feet, so you apply the linear factor twice: the panel is $\frac{3.5}{9}$ square yard. Weight $= \frac{3.5}{9}\text{ yd}^2 \times 50\,\frac{\text{g}}{\text{yd}^2} = \frac{175}{9} \approx 19.44$ grams, which rounds to $19.4$. Type the whole expression, such as 3.5*50/9, so that you round only once, at the end. Students commonly get these wrong answers: 58.3 (dividing by 3 instead of 9), 19.6 or 19.5 (rounding 50/9 partway through), 175 (treating square feet as square yards).

common_errors.why: Applied the linear factor once (3.5 × 50 ÷ 3 ≈ 58.33) instead of squaring it.
Rounded 50 ÷ 9 to 5.6 grams per square foot first, then multiplied by 3.5.
Rounded 50 ÷ 9 to 5.56 first, then multiplied by 3.5 (19.46), which pushes the tenths digit up.
Multiplied 3.5 square feet by 50 grams per square yard, treating the two area units as the same.
